subject: Slimline egress allowlist review for Helix private endpoint
messages:
From: Alex Pierce <alex.pierce@helix.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Helix Security <security@helix.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial: private endpoint egress — minimal allowlist ask

Hi Marissa,

We're kicking off the network review for the Helix private deployment. NetOps needs a "slim" allowlist that we can take to our firewall team — the smaller the surface the better. Can you provide:

- The minimal set of outbound IPs and ports required for Redwood Private control plane (auth, billing, telemetry)
- Any fixed IPs required for the data plane (model inference) vs guidance for FQDN/SNI usage
- Whether TLS termination happens on Redwood side (i.e., do you require TLS inspection) and any mTLS pins
- A short note on IP rotation cadence / ephemeral behaviour we should expect

We want to avoid opening broad CIDRs if possible. We're on AWS in us-east-1 with NAT gateway egress.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m with your infra folks if easier.

Alex
Alex Pierce
Head of Platform Security, Helix Financial
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Pierce <alex.pierce@helix.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: private endpoint egress — minimal allowlist ask

Alex — thanks, and great to meet you (virtually).

Attached is a slimline manifest (helix_allowlist_manifest.csv) and a short summary PDF. High-level answers inline:

- Control plane: we use a small set of stable control-plane IPs for account management, auth, and telemetry. These are the only addresses that must be allowed for the Redwood control plane (see CSV).
- Data plane: for most private deployments we support FQDN+SNI routing for inference traffic; however, customers that require strict IP-only policies can use our dedicated egress pool (static IPs).
- TLS/mTLS: Redwood terminates TLS on our inference runtime. We do not require customers to perform TLS inspection. For Private with VPC peering, we offer optional mTLS on the control plane (certificate exchange) — details in the PDF.
- IP rotation: control-plane IPs are stable (rotated <1% annually); data-plane ephemeral IPs may rotate with autoscaling events unless you opt into the static egress pool.

Follow-ups we need from Helix:
- Confirm whether you can allow FQDNs/SNI.
- Whether you will route via a corporate outbound proxy (we can support mutual TLS to the proxy).
- Any internal maintenance windows / change freeze that affect when we can cut over.

If that sounds good I can schedule a 30m with David (network lead) and Irene (security/compliance) to go through the manifest.

Best,

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Pierce <alex.pierce@helix.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Mar 2028 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: private endpoint egress — minimal allowlist ask

Alex — quick technical clarifications from NetOps perspective:

- Ports: allow outbound 443 to the control-plane IPs. For data-plane inference we recommend outbound 443 to FQDNs; additional ports are not required unless you enable debugging/agent sockets.
- DNS: if you cannot allow FQDNs, we'll provide the static egress pool IPs per-region (these are routable and static while assigned).
- SNI: we support SNI-based allowlisting. If your firewall can allow based on TLS SNI, you can reduce exposure to just our FQDNs.
- Proxy: if you route through a corporate proxy, ensure CONNECT is allowed to our FQDNs and supply proxy intercept certs if you perform TLS inspection; otherwise no changes.

I'll join the call to walk through the NAT/proxy wiring and show a sample iptables/snippets for NAT mapping.

-David
David Kim
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Pierce <alex.pierce@helix.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Helix Security <security@helix.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Mar 2028 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: private endpoint egress — minimal allowlist ask

Thanks Marissa / David — helpful. A couple of clarifying points from our security team:

- We prefer IPs over FQDN rules where possible due to legacy firewall limitations. Can you confirm the static egress pool size and whether it supports per-customer dedicated addresses?
- Is there a signed SLA or attestation on IP stability we can attach to our change board?
- For mTLS on the control plane, can you share the CA bundle and expected CN patterns so our firewall TLS policies can allow handshake passthrough?

We can do the 30m tomorrow 10:00am ET — will that work for your team?

Alex
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Pierce <alex.pierce@helix.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Mar 2028 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: private endpoint egress — minimal allowlist ask

Alex — appreciate the questions. Quick answers:

- Static egress pool: yes, we offer per-customer static egress addresses for Dedicated/Private deployments. Typical pool size for a single tenant starts at 4 IPs; we can increase depending on throughput and subnets you need to advertise.
- Stability attestation: we provide a signed network stability statement as part of the Private deployment package (we'll attach a stamped attestation to the onboarding bundle).
- mTLS CA and CNs: we will provide the CA bundle and expected subject names in a separate secure artifact (we do not send cert material over plain email). For the call we can agree on the handshake expectations and delivery mechanism (SFTP or a secure share).

Next steps:
- I'll upload the signed stability attestation and the CA bundle to the shared Drive link.
- Marissa: please schedule the 30m SRE/NetOps call (tomorrow 10:00am ET / 07:00am PT worked for Helix).

Thanks — Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
